title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 25 (Document Containing Offer of Securities for Sale to Be Deemed Prospectus)

content.overview: Section 25 treats a document by which securities allotted or agreed to be allotted by a company with a view to public sale are offered for sale to the public as a prospectus, so that prospectus obligations cannot be avoided by an offer-for-sale structure.
content.glance: If securities were allotted or agreed to be allotted with a view to public offer for sale, the public offer document is deemed a prospectus.
content.study: Where a company allots or agrees to allot securities with a view to those securities being offered for sale to the public, any document by which the offer for sale is made is deemed to be a prospectus issued by the company. Prospectus enactments and rules apply with the statutory adaptations. There is a rebuttable presumption that an allotment or agreement to allot within a prescribed period before the offer was made with a view to public sale. Current-law framing: identify allotment with a view to public sale; treat the offer document as a prospectus; apply s. 26 and related duties.

sections.heading: Deeming Rule
sections.body: A document offering for sale to the public securities allotted or agreed to be allotted with a view to public sale is deemed a prospectus.

sections.heading: Application of Prospectus Law
sections.body: Prospectus enactments and rules apply with the statutory modifications.

sections.heading: Presumption
sections.body: Allotment or agreement to allot within the prescribed period before the offer is presumed to have been with a view to public sale, subject to proof to the contrary.

provisions.title: Document containing offer of securities for sale to be deemed prospectus

examples.title: Offer for sale after allotment
examples.body: A company allots shares to an intermediary who immediately offers them to the public. The offer document is deemed a prospectus under s. 25.

examples.title: Rebutting the presumption
examples.body: Allotment occurred long before any public offer for an independent purpose. The presumption may be rebutted on the facts.

hypotheticals.question: Can a company avoid prospectus rules by allotting to a middleman who then sells to the public?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Section 25 deems the offer-for-sale document a prospectus where the allotment was with a view to public sale.

distinctions.title: Deemed prospectus (s. 25) vs content of prospectus (s. 26)
distinctions.left: When an offer-for-sale document is treated as a prospectus

misconceptions.trap: Only a document formally labelled prospectus attracts prospectus law.
misconceptions.correction: Section 25 deems certain offer-for-sale documents to be prospectuses regardless of label.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 25 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Identify allotment with a view to public sale. II. Apply the deeming rule. III. Apply prospectus duties. IV. Conclude.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What should submissions contain?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Allotment facts; view to public sale; deeming; prospectus compliance; precise relief.
